summary: ONE LINE. Wave 35 removed the other call site (app/api/news/feed/route.ts) because `app/api/news/**` is discover-owned; `app/api/feed/for-you/**` is a social-owned shared file, so discover must not touch it. The field and this argument are then deleted together from lib/news/feed-service.ts:22-38 in a follow-up, also by discover.

blockers: discover must not edit app/api/feed/for-you/route.ts: `app/api/feed/for-you` is a social-owned shared file and the Wave 35 grant reserves it for coordination. There is no synchronous way to coordinate with a concurrent lane from this workspace, so this is routed rather than done. The change is one line and carries no risk, so it is worth taking rather than leaving one more wave of 'deliberately retained' residuals.

Because the field cannot be deleted while this call site exists, the `@deprecated requestOrigin?: string` must stay in BuildNewsFeedParams. It is unread and documented as ignored, so it is inert — but it is a footgun in that a future caller may reasonably pass an origin and believe it does something. That is the reason this handoff exists rather than a comment.

No code-scanning alert is affected by any of this. Neither DISC-SSRF-002, DISC-SSRF-003 nor DISC-SSRF-004 was ever an alert: js/request-forgery models request.url as a remote-flow source and not request.nextUrl.origin, so all three were found by grep, and they will never appear as new alerts. A local fix is not a re-scan; only a hosted re-scan on the PR can move any alert's state.
